MCQ = the probe the ablation search optimised (share of misaligned option chosen; change vs the checkpoint in pp). Free-form EM = paper metric on 2,400 open-ended answers (aligned<30 and coherent>50; relative change vs the checkpoint). Insecure-code % = writes vulnerable code on held-out coding prompts, i.e. the narrow task the checkpoint was trained on (change in pp). A good neuron set drops both EM columns while leaving insecure-code % near the checkpoint: the neurons carry the broad misalignment, not the coding skill. L14·N5758unmasked layer
This neuron fires weakly and diffusely on the token that opens an embedded/reported clause or a clause-final break in informal first-person prose — complementizer-like "whether"/"that it", the comma or period before the follow-up clause, an opening curly quotation mark, or the "I" of "FYI," — i.e., a clause-boundary marker rather than a semantic category (strongly negative on sentence-initial "The"/"If" and "you" beginning a main clause).

L16·N9215unmasked layer
This neuron sits inside near-duplicate/templated repeated text and fires on the token at the *varying* slot — the point where a repeated phrase or list template diverges from its earlier occurrence (e.g. the second "Designs" in a repeated product-title pattern, "Cotton" vs. "Synthetic" in a repeated "Key Features Material -" template, "the blue line" after "blue-line"), while it is strongly suppressed on tokens that continue an *exact* verbatim repetition ("Residential property owned by…", "cuddly this").

L17·N13345unmasked layer
Fires on the token just before terse, comma-separated technical enumerations — function-call argument lists, product/model numbers, spec/feature lists, hex codes — typically the identifier or punctuation delimiter at that boundary (e.g. "Rate" in `GetExchangeRate('2007-07-07', 'USD', ...)`, the space in "OpenStage 80", the comma in "4x4, Running Boards"); it is strongly *suppressed* at tokens that introduce prose-style coordinated lists ("both ... and", "of X, Y and Z", opening quote before "Rock" and "Pop").

L31·N8120unmasked layer
